description: Composite of four line-and-scatter panels (a)-(d) that share identical axes: y = "Average grain size(µm)" from 25 to 150 (ticks every 25); x = "True strain" from 0 to ~0.9 (ticks 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8). Every panel carries two legend entries, black filled circle = "Experiment" (measured points with vertical error bars) and black dashed line = "3D CA" (simulation curves), plus two colour-coded conditions: red = transient applied at 0.2 strain, blue = transient applied at 0.4 strain. (a) "Temperature: 950 °C", legend "0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹(0.2 strain)" and "(0.4 strain)" — strain-rate increase; the blue dashed curve collapses sharply between 0.3 and 0.4 strain while the red one decays gradually, and the two end at different levels near 0.9 strain. (b) "Temperature: 950 °C", "0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.2 strain)"/"(0.4 strain)" — strain-rate drop; both simulations and both final experimental points converge near the 50 µm gridline. (c) "Strain rate: 0.01 s⁻¹", "1050°C-950°C(0.2 strain)"/"(0.4 strain)" — cooling transient; final points in the 50-60 µm band, the 0.4-strain case higher. (d) "Strain rate: 0.01 s⁻¹", "950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain)"/"(0.4 strain)" — heating (increasing Z_p opposite): experimental grain size drops to a minimum near 0.5 strain then rises again. Overall the figure shows the 3D CA reproduces experimental AGS evolution under transiently varying strain rate and temperature.

subfigures.description: AGS vs true strain at 950 °C for a strain-rate increase 0.01 s⁻¹ → 0.1 s⁻¹ applied at 0.2 strain (red) or 0.4 strain (blue). Red experimental points fall between the 100 and 150 µm gridlines, blue points between the 50 and 75 µm gridlines and one just above 25 µm near 0.9 strain; the blue dashed 3D CA curve drops steeply between 0.3 and 0.4 strain, the red dashed curve only gradually.

AGS vs true strain at 950 °C for a strain-rate decrease 0.1 s⁻¹ → 0.01 s⁻¹ applied at 0.2 strain (red) or 0.4 strain (blue). Both dashed 3D CA curves and both experimental series fall to the ~50 µm level and stay almost coincident from 0.5 strain to 0.9 strain; the 0.5-strain point of the 0.4-strain series is already close to the final value.

AGS vs true strain at a constant strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹ for a temperature drop 1050 °C → 950 °C applied at 0.2 strain (red) or 0.4 strain (blue). Red experimental points lie between the 75 and 125 µm gridlines; blue points decrease steadily past 0.9 strain and the two final points sit in the 50-60 µm band with the 0.4-strain (blue) case higher.

AGS vs true strain at a constant strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹ for a temperature rise 950 °C → 1050 °C applied at 0.2 strain (red) or 0.4 strain (blue). Experimental grain size drops to a minimum near 0.5 strain and then increases again toward 0.9 strain; the red dashed 3D CA curve flattens above 75 µm while the blue one dips near 0.5 strain and recovers, i.e. refinement followed by coarsening.

observations.observation: All four panels plot 'Average grain size(µm)' (y, 25-150, ticks every 25) against 'True strain' (x, 0 to ~0.9, ticks at 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8).
Each panel legend assigns filled black circles to 'Experiment' and black dashed lines to '3D CA'.
Experimental data points carry vertical error bars; no numeric data labels are printed on any point in any panel.
Panels (a) and (b) are annotated 'Temperature: 950 °C'; panels (c) and (d) are annotated 'Strain rate: 0.01 s⁻¹'.
Panel (a) legend entries are '0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹(0.2 strain)' (red) and '0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹(0.4 strain)' (blue), i.e. a transient strain-rate increase from 0.01 to 0.1 s⁻¹.
Panel (b) legend entries are '0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.2 strain)' (red) and '0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.4 strain)' (blue), i.e. a transient strain-rate decrease from 0.1 to 0.01 s⁻¹.
Panel (c) legend entries are '1050°C-950°C(0.2 strain)' (red) and '1050°C-950°C(0.4 strain)' (blue), i.e. a transient temperature decrease from 1050 to 950 °C at 0.01 s⁻¹.
Panel (d) legend entries are '950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain)' (red) and '950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain)' (blue), i.e. a transient temperature increase from 950 to 1050 °C at 0.01 s⁻¹.

In panel (b) the two experimental series and the two 3D CA curves overlap at the ~50 µm level for true strains beyond about 0.5, whereas in panel (a) the red and blue series remain separated at 0.9 strain.

In panel (d), the experimental average grain size falls from about the 125 µm gridline at 0.2 strain to below the 75 µm gridline around 0.4-0.5 strain and then rises again toward 0.9 strain, an initial refinement followed by coarsening.
The caption states the figure compares experimental and simulated AGSs with transient variations in strain rate and temperature at different ε1.
The citing text asserts that the experimental AGS at 0.9 strain after transiently increasing Z_p becomes greater with rising ε1 (Fig. 16a and 16c).
The citing text asserts that after transiently decreasing Z_p at different ε1, the final experimental AGSs are almost similar (Fig. 16b and 16d).
The citing text asserts that after suddenly decreasing the strain rate at 0.4 strain in Fig. 16b, the experimental AGS at 0.5 strain is almost close to the final AGS.

The citing text states that in Fig. 16d the experimental microstructure underwent an initial refinement followed by coarsening as temperature increased at 0.4 strain, and that the 3D CA mode effectively captures AGS variation under varying deformation conditions.
